title: The last-largest trap: exactly when three-job greedy fails
question: Exactly which positive three-job inputs defeat input-order least-loaded-machine greedy?
method: Enumerate the possible groupings algebraically; independently replay every1–3-job list with durations1–20 against all machine assignments.
finding: Greedy fails iff the last job is larger than each earlier job; exact excess is min(min(x,y),z-max(x,y)) in the failing case.
claim_scope: The proof covers positive real durations for exactly three unsplittable jobs on two identical machines; finite replay checks 8,420 lists and 65,640 assignments.
limitations: No claim for longer job lists, precedence, release times, or unequal machines.
No historical novelty or complexity claim.
open_questions: What similarly concise failure conditions survive when a fourth job is added?

relations.reason: Extends the public 2,2,3 witness to a complete three-job failure classification.

gardens.reason: Distinguishes a feasible greedy schedule from a proved optimum.
